name: Drum Kit
shortDescription: Multi-component percussion set combining struck membranes and metallic cymbals for rhythmic timekeeping.
description: The drum kit is a multi-component percussion system combining membranophones (drums) and idiophones (cymbals). Each component produces a distinct timbral profile: the kick drum delivers subwoofer-range fundamentals through a large membrane; the snare produces a sharp crack via snare wires against the bottom head; toms provide mid-frequency accents; cymbals create broad-spectrum inharmonic noise bursts and sustained shimmer.
historicalOrigins: The modern drum kit emerged in early 20th-century New Orleans jazz, where a single player using foot pedals (invented 1909) could combine multiple percussion instruments previously requiring several drummers.
acousticPrinciples: Circular membrane vibration: Chladni/Bessel mode patterns (J₀, J₁, J₂) determine resonant frequencies
Snare wires create additional overtones via sympathetic rattle against bottom drumhead
Cymbals: bronze alloy plates produce inharmonic vibration modes characteristic of metallic idiophones
Kick drum coupling to floor and low-frequency air radiation through front port

characteristics.pitchRange: Kick: 60–100 Hz; Snare: 200–300 Hz; Toms: 80–300 Hz; Cymbals: 300 Hz – 8 kHz
characteristics.orchestralRole: Rhythmic timekeeper, groove foundation, dynamic accents

soundDNA.exciter: Drumstick, mallet, or brush striking membrane or metallic plate
soundDNA.attackDecay: Impulsive attack (< 1ms), fast exponential decay (50ms–2s by component)
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Bright crack (snare), deep thud (kick), shimmering wash (cymbals)
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Omnidirectional from drum heads; directional from hi-hat edges

kick.label: Kick Drum (Bass Drum)
kick.function: 22" diameter kick drum producing low-frequency pulse (60–100 Hz) via foot-operated beater.

characteristics.material: Maple shell, Mylar batter head, felt beater
characteristics.mechanism: Large membrane Bessel mode J₀ (fundamental dominant)

snare.label: Snare Drum
snare.function: 14" drum with steel snare wires on bottom head creating distinctive crack on backbeat.

characteristics.material: Steel/aluminium shell, Coated batter head, steel snare wires
characteristics.mechanism: Top head drives air column which snaps snare wires

toms.label: Tom-Toms
toms.function: Two rack toms (10",12") and one floor tom (14") for pitched melodic fills.

characteristics.material: Maple shells with transparent/coated batter heads
characteristics.mechanism: Two-headed cylindrical resonators with tunable pitch

hi_hat.label: Hi-Hat Cymbals
hi_hat.function: Pair of 14" cymbals on stand. Foot pedal controls open/closed gap, changing timbre.

crash.label: Crash Cymbal
crash.function: 16–18" crash cymbal for strong accents. Tapered edge produces explosive high-frequency burst.

ride.label: Ride Cymbal
ride.function: 20–22" heavy ride cymbal providing clear 'ping' on the bell and controlled wash on the bow.

characteristics.material: Heavy-cast B20 bronze with raised bell
characteristics.mechanism: Localised bell radiation vs. broad-plate modes

followTheSound.title: Low-Frequency Pulse
followTheSound.explanation: Foot pedal drives felt beater into batter head. Large membrane (J₀ mode) pushes air column.

followTheSound.title: Snare Crack
followTheSound.explanation: Stick strikes batter head; air pulse snaps snare wires on resonant head, adding broad-spectrum noise.

followTheSound.title: Rhythmic Timekeeping
followTheSound.explanation: Open/closed hi-hat creates alternating washy/tight metallic articulation patterns.

followTheSound.title: Dynamic Accent
followTheSound.explanation: Full-arm strike on crash creates explosive inharmonic cymbal bloom decaying over 1–3 seconds.
